item.title: Able Prom celebrated at the Royal Sonesta
item.description: NAWILIWILI — When doors to the Royal Sonesta Kauai Resort opened on Feb. 7 for the Kauai Able Prom, there were more than 100 guests welcomed in “true red-carpet style,” said Ana Munoz, an Able Ministries volunteer and coordinator of the 12th annual event.

item.title: U.S. Archbishop will be beatified, one step away from sainthood
item.description: The Vatican will allow an American archbishop, who was one of the best-known Catholic clergy of the last century, to be beatified, ending a six-year delay and placing him one step away from sainthood.

item.title: EDITORIAL: No public funding of private benefits
item.description: In what world would public funding be used to cover private workers’ paid holiday off? Let it not be in Hawaii.

item.title: Gambling bills struggle to remain alive amid Hawaii’s prohibition on wagering
item.description: A bill that would allow cruise ship gambling — even while ships are docked in Hawaii ports — stalled in a House committee Wednesday while another bill that would allow sports betting squeaked through as the state Legislature continues to debate whether to end Hawaii’s prohibition on gambling.

item.title: Water system upgrade work on Ahukini Road
item.description: LIHUE — The Department of Water and contractor Cushnie Construction Company Inc. will perform water system upgrade work on Ahukini Road near the main entrance to the Lihue Airport on Thursday, from 9 a.m. to 3 p.m., weather permitting. This water service shutdown is not expected to impact customers in the area, including the Lihue Airport.

item.title: Hawaii attorney general moves forward with corruption probe
item.description: Lt. Gov. Sylvia Luke refuses to say whether she has been subpoenaed or interviewed by state law enforcement as part of a criminal public corruption probe into an unidentified state lawmaker who took allegedly received $35,000 in a paper bag while being recorded by an FBI informant.

item.title: Superheroes wear quilts
item.description: LIHUE — “Superheros don’t wear capes,” said quilter Toni Waas. “They wear quilts!”

item.title: Kung Hee Fat Choy! Welcome the Year of the Fire Horse!
item.description: LIHUE — Today is the start of the Chinese (or Lunar) New Year welcoming the Year of the Horse, according to the Chinese lunar calendar.

item.title: Malasada Tuesday!
item.description: LIHUE — Tiffany Lum of the Kauai Menehune Kitchen said on Monday that the wind at the Pau Hana Market was not the problem.
